newsitem.title: USA: Fla. Supreme Court to hear Bucs bonds case May 9.
newsitem.headline: Fla. Supreme Court to hear Bucs bonds case May 9.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court set a hearing for May 9 at 0900 EDT on an appeal to block a $204.5 million bond issue for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' new stadium, the court clerk said Thursday.

The Tampa Sports Authority bond sale, initially set for November, has been repeatedly delayed by legal wrangling. Former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe sued to block the sale, saying it would illegally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit football team.

Hillsborough County Judge Sam Pendino refused to validate the bonds, agreeing that a lease provision giving the Bucs the first $2 million in non-Bucs revenues from the stadium made the project one primarily for private gain.
But Pendino said he would approve the bonds if a revised lease agreement was submitted by Friday. That deadline became moot when Poe appealed to the state Supreme Court.
Hillsborough County voters approved a one-cent sales tax hike in September for schools, public safety and debt service on the stadium bonds.
